newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields fall, crown ends firmer.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields fall, crown ends firmer.

text.p: The crown firmed substantially and debt yields fell across the curve on Tuesday aided by stronger foreign markets.
At 1500 GMT the crown stood at 4.4760 against the mark compared to 4.5170 late on Monday. It had peaked at 4.4640.
Dealers said the appetite of foreign players had grown and a major hedge fund was seen in the market.
"One player made a major amount which was a hit. The 4.49/4.50 level, which was previously the floor for the crown against mark, has now become the ceiling," one dealer said.
Another dealer said budget details had been leaked.

"Information has leaked from the spring budget and the market sees that at least it does not look worse than expected," he said. "At the same time the dollar hikes further up. I think the crown will firm to 4.45 even if it stopped a bit right now."
Six-month T-bill rates shed four basis points to 4.11 percent and the ten-year bond yield dropped 11 to 7.15 percent.
The Riksbank kept the repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent as expected. In the afternoon it said it will use straight repos rather than reverse from April 15 for liquidity reasons.
